meta.title: Ukrainian B2 Upper Intermediate
meta.subtitle: 1500 words · both directions, as two cards per word
meta.desc: Both study directions in one deck: Ukrainian → English (see the Ukrainian, recall the meaning) and English → Ukrainian (see an English meaning, recall the Ukrainian). Each direction is a card of its own with its own schedule, so recognising a word and producing it are learnt separately. 1500 words for an upper-intermediate learner, aligned to B2 of the Common European Framework of Reference, whose global descriptor begins 'Can understand the main ideas of complex text on both concrete and abstract topics, including technical discussions in their field of specialisation' — a learner here is able to interact with a degree of fluency and spontaneity that makes regular interaction with native speakers quite possible without strain for either party, and to produce clear, detailed text on a wide range of subjects and explain a viewpoint on a topical issue giving the advantages and disadvantages of various options. The words already taught by the levels below this one are left out. WHERE THESE WORDS COME FROM, since it matters: Ukraine certifies proficiency in the language but publishes no graded word list, so this deck is not any examination's vocabulary and does not claim to be. It is assembled from two things that can be stated. 347 of the 1500 come from a vocabulary written for the level's scope — the economy and business, the workplace, government, law and rights, science and technology, the environment and energy, society and its problems, the media, education and the mind, health and medicine, culture, history and identity, the arts and reviewing them, attitudes and character, the words that build an argument, and the verbs of change and judgement — and the other 1153 are the commonest remaining words of everyday Ukrainian, taken from a frequency list built from film and television subtitles and counted by the WHOLE word, every form of a noun or a verb added together. The cards are dealt by that frequency, so the words you meet most often come first. Every headword is printed in Cyrillic with its stress marked (кни́га, роблю́), because Ukrainian stress can fall on any syllable and move as the word changes, and nothing else shows it; there is no transliteration, and the Ukrainian Alphabet deck, the first in this collection, teaches the letters. The 763 nouns show their gender, their genitive and their plural; the 416 verbs show their aspect, imperfective or perfective, with the other verb of the pair beside them, their я and він forms and their past; and behind the All forms fold every noun's seven cases and every verb's tenses by person. Real example sentences come with 1377 of the 1500 words, three apiece for 1191 of them, with the word picked out in colour and a speaker beside the sentence and the headword. Sources. Level: the Common European Framework of Reference (Council of Europe), global scale. Meanings, gender, aspect, stress and forms: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Frequency: a word list built from OpenSubtitles (hermitdave/FrequencyWords, CC BY-SA 4.0). Example sentences: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR.
